tagline: The engine's own test map: a row of plain rooms, one per system under test, from stairs and platforms to props and characters.
overview:
Red Test Lab is a deliberately basic map that RedEngine's developers use to check the engine's systems. It is a long building of plain, colour-coded rooms in a row: a spawn hall, a clearance room of tall panels to squeeze between, a vertical room with stairs and a raised platform, a props room with crates and a ladder, a range with targets, and a characters room.

There is no game here: it exists so that movement, collisions, climbing and the engine's props can be tested in isolation. It is on this site because it is part of the engine's content, and it can be fun to poke at.
story: No story: this is a test facility. It was built so the engine's developers (and the AI agents that work on the engine) can check movement, collisions, climbing and physics props one room at a time.
goal: There is no goal: it is a test map.
rules: Each room tests one thing: spawning, squeezing through gaps, stairs and platforms, loose props, a target range and character models.
Your bat can knock the loose props around.
Nothing is scored and there is no time limit.
